changes.wohChoice: an officer (ASV-baseline; the court-official sense; the literal eunuch-sense and its tension with Potifar's marriage documented in commentary). Context clause (isaiah-woh wave I-6): 'eunuch(s)' in Isaiah, where the context favours the castration sense: 39:7 (the king's own sons taken to serve in a foreign palace; ASV, KJV, NJPS 'eunuchs') and, as a forward commitment, 56:3-4 ('Behold, I am a dry tree'; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'eunuch'). The parallel 2 Kgs 20:18 follows Isa 39:7 when it is translated.

rationaleAppend: Isaiah 39:7 (isaiah-woh wave I-6): wᵉhāyû sārîsîm bᵉhêḵal meleḵ bāḇel 'and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon'. ASV, KJV and NJPS print 'eunuchs'; JPS 1917 prints 'officers' here and at 2 Kgs 20:18 (bible-api.com and Sefaria API v3, checked 2026-11-27). At 2 Kgs 20:18 Fox, The Early Prophets (2014), has 'officials' (with hêḵāl 'the Great-Hall') and the Metsudah Tanach has 'officers' (Sefaria API v3, checked 2026-11-27), so three checked versions take the court-official reading. The Genesis tension that decided 'an officer' at Gen 37:36 / 39:1 (a married Potiphar) is absent: the sārîsîm are Hezekiah's own sons taken to serve a foreign king, the setting in which the versions that print 'eunuchs' read the castration sense. Isa 56:3-4 makes the sense explicit, since the sārîs fears he is 'a dry tree' (ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS 'a withered tree'; checked), and the context clause fixes 'eunuch' there in advance so that Isaiah's two sārîs passages share one English word. The court-official sense is recorded in the 39:7 commentary. The claim_type stays inferred: the choice of sense remains contextual, as at the Genesis sites, and JPS 1917, Fox and Metsudah show that the functional reading is defended at this passage too.

Isaiah 39:1 (isaiah-woh wave I-6): sᵉp̄ārîm ûminḥāh 'letters and a present', the diplomatic gift of the king of Babylon to Hezekiah that the rationale above already lists with 2 Kgs 20:12. 'A present' follows ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS has 'a gift' (checked 2026-11-27). The inter-political register is the operative one, and 'tribute' is not used, because nothing in the context makes the gift a payment owed by a vassal.

Isaiah application (isaiah-woh wave I-6): at Isa 39:7 bᵉhêḵal meleḵ bāḇel is 'in the palace of the king of Babylon' under this entry's context clause (a human king's residence), with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (checked 2026-11-27). The isaiah-woh overlay entry heikhal-temple-palace-isaiah, which renders 'the temple' at 6:1 and 44:28, carries the same context clause.
